objectives.wording: Explain homeostatic disruption after injury and link metabolic changes to major mediators.
Compare how injury severity, nutrition, infection and comorbidity affect the metabolic response.
Map assessment, optimization, intraoperative coordination and postoperative recovery.
Compare perioperative needs for representative procedures and identify prevention and monitoring priorities.
Compare shock types and justify resuscitation, fluid replacement and monitoring priorities.
Recognize shock in representative cases and explain cause-directed initial treatment principles.
Explain treatment, prognosis and uncertainty empathetically to a simulated patient or family.
Match components to representative indications and recognize major transfusion complications.
Observe an approved transfusion and document identity checks, monitoring and escalation procedures.
Discuss benefits, risks and alternatives to transfusion and explain donation in simulation.
Present a focused history and examination and link findings to burn pathophysiology.
Classify burn type and depth, estimate extent and justify initial care and referral priorities.
Identify medico-legal concerns and document findings and circumstances in a simulated case.
Discuss expected recovery, rehabilitation and uncertainty with a simulated patient and family.
Sequence healing phases and explain local and systemic factors that impair repair.
Elicit, document and present a structured history of a simulated wound.
Distinguish representative wounds, justify management and describe observed care.
Distinguish observed findings from opinion and explain documentation and evidence custody.
Classify surgical infections by source and explain representative mechanisms and risks.
Distinguish prophylaxis from treatment and justify antimicrobial selection and source control in a simulated case.
Define standards and indicators, compare sample outcomes and outline improvement and re-audit.
Develop a focused surgical question and outline design, ethics, measurement and analysis.
Apply ethical principles to representative surgical decisions and consent dilemmas.
Demonstrate respectful communication, privacy and empathy during a simulated surgical encounter.
Analyze documentation, disclosure and accountability in simulated surgical cases using applicable guidance.
Select biochemical, microbiological, pathological and imaging tests and interpret representative results.
Explain the biological rationale for early detection and map multidisciplinary decision-making.
Explain simulated results and next steps in plain language and check understanding.
Obtain consent in simulation after discussing indication, material risks, benefits and alternatives.
Document observations of common and emergency procedures and demonstrate an assigned role in supervised minor surgery.
Demonstrate first aid, suturing and representative minor procedures on a simulator.
Assess patient and procedural risks and explain optimization and escalation criteria.
Compare general, regional and local techniques by purpose, suitability and risks.
Demonstrate basic airway maintenance and reassessment on a mannequin.
Identify appropriate candidates and explain preparation, discharge and safety requirements.
Compare acute postoperative and chronic pain approaches and explain reassessment and adverse-effect monitoring.
Apply identity, site, procedural checks and team communication to a simulated operation.
Identify causes and explain effects on healing, complications and recovery.
Estimate requirements and losses and justify replacement and reassessment in sample cases.
Compare oral, enteral and parenteral routes by indications, monitoring and complications.
Explain graft recognition, rejection and the principles of compatibility.
Compare representative indications and surgical principles and explain immunosuppression and follow-up.
Use applicable official guidance to analyze consent, allocation and safeguards in a simulated donation case.
Role-play a sensitive discussion with patients or relatives and respond to questions without pressure.
Distinguish aseptic technique, disinfection and sterilization and select methods for representative settings.
Demonstrate sterile preparation and wound suturing on a simulator.
Match incisions and instruments to intended exposure and operative purpose.
Compare sutures, needles and knots and explain how tissue and purpose guide technique.
Classify representative waste and match it to disposal pathways using local procedures.
Compare representative indications, benefits and limitations with open approaches.
Explain scene safety, initial assessment and immediate priorities in representative injuries.
Demonstrate BLS and coordinated transport of an injured person in simulation.
Explain triage, command, communication and resource allocation in a mass casualty scenario.
Compare injury mechanisms and explain primary and secondary brain injury.
Select investigations and justify observation, intervention and escalation in a simulated head injury.
Interpret clinical findings and calculate and document the Glasgow Coma Scale from a simulated head injury case.
Identify injury patterns and justify investigations and initial management.
Explain how blunt and penetrating trauma compromise ventilation or circulation.
Recognize major chest injury patterns and prioritize initial management and escalation.
Demonstrate airway maintenance and recognition and initial management of tension pneumothorax, haemothorax and flail chest.
Compare representative infections by mechanism, findings and management priorities.
Classify common benign and malignant lesions and justify representative management pathways.
Demonstrate examination and propose investigations and treatment for a simulated swelling.
Explain developmental causes and classify representative cleft lip and palate patterns.
Outline staged reconstruction goals and multidisciplinary care.
Relate risk factors to pathogenesis and recognize representative symptoms and signs.
Select investigations and explain stage-based treatment principles.
Relate surgical anatomy to obstructive, inflammatory and neoplastic presentations.
Choose investigations and justify treatment principles for representative disorders.
Map relevant thyroid relations, blood supply and physiology to surgical decisions.
Compare mechanisms of diffuse enlargement and nodules.
Demonstrate and document the clinical examination of a thyroid swelling, then discuss its differential diagnosis and management.
Classify major types and compare presentations and management.
Locate typical and ectopic glands and explain their operative relevance.
Explain the presentation and management principles of hyperparathyroidism.
Explain the presentation and management principles of hypoparathyroidism.
Map relations and vascular supply relevant to adrenal surgery.
Relate causes and presentations to management principles in representative cases.
Select biochemical and imaging assessment and justify management pathways.
Map breast anatomy and lymphatic drainage and select investigations for representative symptoms.
Compare causes, presentations and management of common benign and infectious conditions.
Distinguish benign and malignant presentations and explain investigation and treatment principles.
Counsel a simulated patient on options and obtain informed consent.
Demonstrate systematic palpation and describe a simulated mass.
Explain the role of surgery in coronary, valvular and congenital heart disease.
Recognize representative presentations and explain management principles by compartment and cause.
Relate risk factors and pathogenesis to presentation and management pathways.
Compare mechanisms, presentations, investigations and management of representative hernias.
Demonstrate examination and distinguish representative hernia types in simulation.
Recognize clinical patterns and connect likely causes to complications and initial management.
Compare abscess, mesenteric cyst and retroperitoneal tumour by mechanism, findings, tests and treatment principles.
Relate oesophageal landmarks, blood supply and motility to surgical disease.
Compare benign and malignant presentations and justify investigations and management.
Relate gastric blood supply, innervation and physiology to surgical disease.
Compare causes, presentations, tests and management in representative cases.
Demonstrate a focused examination for a simulated gastric presentation.
Use applied liver anatomy to compare presentations, tests and treatment of abscess, hydatid disease, trauma and tumours.
Use splenic anatomy to justify assessment and treatment and explain infection prevention after splenectomy.
Use biliary anatomy and presentation to select investigations and management pathways.
Relate bowel segments, vascular territories and mesenteric attachments to surgical presentations.
Compare representative small and large bowel disorders, including neonatal obstruction and short bowel syndrome.
Recognize typical and atypical appendicitis, complications and appropriate investigations and care.
Map relevant rectal and anal landmarks and explain representative congenital anomalies.
Distinguish common presentations and justify investigations and management.
Demonstrate examination, interpret findings and propose tests and treatment in simulation.
Demonstrate prostate examination on a mannequin and document findings.
Classify causes and justify investigation and management by presentation.
Compare representative congenital anomalies by presentation, investigation and treatment.
Distinguish representative presentations and justify testing and management.
Identify probable obstruction and justify imaging and management.
Relate stone location and complications to presentation, investigation and management.
Compare representative findings and justify imaging and treatment pathways.
Distinguish acute from chronic retention and explain initial management and follow-up.
Recognize representative presentations and explain investigations and treatment.
Explain the presentation of benign prostatic hyperplasia and justify its assessment and care.
Explain the presentation of prostatitis and justify its assessment and care.
Distinguish prostate cancer from benign prostatic disease and justify its assessment and care.
Recognize obstructive symptoms and explain investigation and management.
Distinguish phimosis and paraphimosis and justify care and referral.
Recognise penile carcinoma and justify care and referral.
Relate descent anatomy to presentation, assessment and management.
Use anatomy and clinical findings to distinguish infection from urgent alternatives and justify investigations and care.
Describe the applied anatomy, clinical features, investigations and principles of management of varicocele.
Compare types by anatomy, presentation, investigations and care.
Classify major types and explain recognition, investigations and treatment principles.
